verdict.rationale: Codex's own docs describe the full flow: start a cloud task from GitLab or Linear issues, run it in an isolated environment configured for the repository, then review the diff and open a pull request when the result is ready. missing for 10: GitHub Issues as a documented trigger (only GitHub pull requests are listed), detail on whether the PR links back to or closes the originating issue, PR opening appears to be a user-initiated step rather than automatic, and no independent or hands-on corroboration of the issue-to-PR flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn a tracked issue into a complete pull request end-to-end

citations.quote: Start work in Codex cloud from GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests and issues, Linear issues, or Slack channels and threads.
Run tasks in isolated cloud environments, work in parallel, and start work from the web, GitHub, GitLab, Linear, or Slack.
Configure the dependencies, tools, variables, and setup steps each repository needs.
Inspect the summary and diff, request a follow-up, or open a pull request when the result is ready.
Delegate a longer task and return when it is ready.
